summary: Independently verified Phase .1R.5's mechanism-neutral HPAC verifier (src/pcae/core/hpac_verifier.py) against HUMAN_PRINCIPAL_AUTHENTICATION_CONTRACT.md (HPAC-001 v2.0), re-deriving HPAC-REQ-054's ten-step sequence directly from the contract text before comparing it to the implementation. VERDICT: NOT VERIFIED -- AUTHENTICATED-PRINCIPAL RESULT AUTHORITY DEFECT. BLOCKING finding F1: AuthenticatedHumanPrincipal's HPAC-REQ-056 trusted-construction seal is enforced only inside __init__; the class defines no __new__ override, so object.__new__(AuthenticatedHumanPrincipal) allocates a fully-populated, isinstance-true instance -- including is_real_runtime_eligible == True at PRODUCTION assurance -- without ever running verify_human_authentication. Independently reproduced via direct interactive probe outside the test suite. Currently non-exploitable in production: zero consumers of hpac_verifier.py / AuthenticatedHumanPrincipal exist anywhere in src/pcae (confirmed by grep and by re-running the existing AST-based zero-consumer test), so no live code path can reach a forged instance today -- but the construction boundary the module and HPAC-REQ-056 claim to enforce is not actually closed. Non-blocking findings: F2, HPAC-REQ-054 step 4 (independent challenge_digest recomputation from canonical challenge state) is not implemented, only a string-equality cross-check deferred into step 9's lifecycle-binding logic, bounded by the foundation having no standalone canonical Challenge store yet; F3, this traces to .1R.4's own planning document mislabeling HPAC-REQ-054 as an eight-step algorithm and silently dropping contract step 4 in its own re-derivation -- pre-existing debt from an already-closed phase, not introduced by .1R.5, but its consequence propagated into .1R.5's and .1R.5's phase report's claim of ten-step fidelity; F4, tests/test_hpac_verifier.py::test_caller_constructed_verifier_result_rejected overclaims relative to what it proves (only the __init__-wrong-seal path, never object.__new__). All other trust-bearing areas independently verified clean: canonical-resolution-only input handling for principal/credential/presentation/proof, UP and UV checked as genuinely independent booleans, anti-transfer/invocation-binding, non-serializability (pickle, deepcopy, and shallow-copy all raise TypeError), deterministic NON-REAL assurance classification with no caller-driven upgrade path, zero PB/runtime-authority/Gate-9 imports (AST-confirmed), B1/B7/N1/N2 files untouched since the .1R.4 baseline (817b788a). Added tests/test_hpac_verifier_independent_verification_3w1r2b1r1115a1.py, a fresh 29-test independently-derived adversarial suite (not copied from the existing .1R.5 tests): 27 pass, 2 correctly fail (documenting F1 as the contract-required behavior rather than being adjusted to match the implementation). Existing 27 .1R.5 tests re-run unmodified, still pass. No repair of F1-F4 performed (explicitly out of scope for this verification phase); no B1/B7/N1/N2 repair; no PB/runtime-authority integration; no real FIDO2 or protected-UI work. Recommends a narrow follow-up blocking-repair phase closing the object.__new__ construction-boundary gap, pending separate explicit human authorization and formal phase-ID assignment -- not pre-assigned by this phase per its own no-invent-an-ID constraint.
derived_correctness: HPAC-REQ-054's ten-step sequence was independently re-extracted directly from docs/contracts/HUMAN_PRINCIPAL_AUTHENTICATION_CONTRACT.md section 18 before re-reading hpac_verifier.py's implementation a second time, per the governing prompt's re-derive-do-not-trust instruction. This independent derivation surfaced that .1R.4's own planning document mislabels the sequence as eight steps and silently drops contract step 4 -- a defect neither .1R.4 nor .1R.5 caught because both relied on the planning document's paraphrase rather than the contract text. The object.__new__ construction-boundary defect (F1) was found by direct interactive Python-level probing against the installed module (not inferred from reading code alone), then captured as two failing pytest assertions in the fresh suite, and independently reproduced a third time outside any test harness during this metadata's authoring to confirm the finding was not a fixture artifact.
